Set up complete. Summary of the module (`syscli`, in this directory):

- **`main.go`** — entry point calling a single `SystemLoad() (string, error)` function.
- **`syscall_linux.go`** (`//go:build linux` via filename) — uses `unix.Sysinfo` for uptime.
- **`syscall_darwin.go`** — uses `unix.ClockGettime(unix.CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW, ...)`.
- **`syscall_windows.go`** — loads `GetTickCount64` via `windows.NewLazySystemDLL`, since `x/sys/windows` doesn't wrap it directly.

Each file implements the same `SystemLoad` signature; the build's filename suffix (`_linux`, `_darwin`, `_windows`) picks the right one automatically — no manual build tags needed. Verified `go build`/`go vet` succeed for `linux/amd64`, `darwin/arm64`, and `windows/amd64`, and ran the linux binary for a sanity check (`uptime: 38h7m52s`).

This is a minimal skeleton — swap in whatever real syscalls your CLI needs; the three-file-per-OS + shared-signature pattern is the reusable part.
